description: Intent i010 (snapshot s03, branch debugfs-write-memdup-sscanf) complete with 7 reported findings. (1) drivers/net/ethernet/brocade/bna/bnad_debugfs.c:315 (regrd) and :375 (regwr): debugfs write handlers perform kern_buf = memdup_user(buf, nbytes) allocating exactly nbytes bytes with no NUL terminator, then sscanf(kern_buf, "%x:%x", ...) which scans until NUL past the allocation — the direct structural twin of the scsi bfa seed (same Brocade BFA driver family, same fix primitive memdup_user_nul). (2) drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_debugfs.c:174/260/335/431: four fwlog debugfs write handlers (module, nr_messages, enable, log_size) do memdup_user(buf, count) with count bounded to 8/4/2/5 then sscanf(cmd_buf, "%s", user_val) on the unterminated heap buffer — OOB read plus unbounded %s copy into 8/16-byte stack arrays, and cmd_buf is leaked. (3) drivers/scsi/qedf/qedf_debugfs.c:173: qedf_dbg_debug_cmd_write does memdup_user(buffer, count) then kstrtouint(kern_buf, 10, &val), whose lib/kstrtox.c contract requires a null-terminated string; unterminated input walks past the allocation. Evidence: literal source quotes verified in-tree; all listed candidates classified reported/safe/unresolved; negative examples verified (rvu_debugfs.c:1002 uses memdup_user(buffer, count + 1) plus cmd_buf[count]='\0' terminator; hfi1/qib/wil6210/rtw89/wfx/wlcore/mlx5/bpmp/nvram sites consume raw bytes with explicit lengths and no string API). Limitations: search bounded to memdup_user-family call sites and debugfs/debug-control write handlers; kmalloc+copy_from_user debugfs variants not exhaustively enumerated; rvu_dbg_lf_reset_write unverified; findings are source-structure hypotheses, no KASAN runtime reproduction; all require root/debugfs access and respective hardware (BNA NIC, Intel ice PF, QLogic FC adapter).
